title: refactor(ci): split lint/test/release workflows, optimize cache & parallelism
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Our monolithic CI workflow has grown slow and fragile (10-18m for PRs) and it's increasingly causing flakiness during release automation. This PR splits the large combined workflow into three focused pipelines (lint, test, release), standardizes cache keys, and tunes job-level parallelism to reduce queue times and improve cache hit rates. Key goals: 1) Reduce PR CI median time-to-green by ~40%, 2) improve incremental cache reuse across matrix runs, 3) reduce load on runners during peak merges, 4) make release workflow more auditable and retry-friendly. Changes: - Introduce .github/workflows/lint.yml, .github/workflows/test.yml, .github/workflows/release.yml (extracted from the previous combined workflow). - Consolidate reusable steps into .github/workflows/actions/common.yml and move shared setup into scripts/ci/setup.sh. - Implement deterministic cache keys for node_modules, pnpm store, and build artifacts (hash of package-lock + lockfileVersion + workspace list). - Reduce matrix dimension duplication (separate fast lint-only jobs from heavy integration test jobs). - Add targeted parallelism controls for test matrix jobs and a dynamic batch size script (scripts/ci/parallelism.py) that reads CI_PARALLELISM_HINT from job labels. - Bump several GitHub Actions to pinned versions for stability (actions/checkout@v4, pnpm/action-setup@v2, actions/cache@v4). - Add opt-in fallback cache behavior for flaky cache uploads (best-effort upload, don't fail the job). See linked Linear: ENG-1245, ENG-1399 for perf targets and release automation scope. Checklist: - [x] Extract workflows and validate synthetic runs - [x] Add deterministic cache key logic - [x] Validate parallelism tuning on canary repo - [x] Add documentation and upgrade notes - [x] Run full integration pipeline on merge Notes: The description below summarizes the high-level diffs and rationale; full workflow YAMLs are included in the patch.
